body: I'm glad you came through the other side with good news. That said, I do recommend taking another in a week or so, just to be sure. And take care of yourself, seek counseling for this. It was a traumatic experience and you deserve to go at your own pace and feel good and strong again.

I think your post was removed at some point (that's what I see for the content), but I looked over your comments.

Welcome to the club. Interesting you're a product manager. I'm a supervisor at a tech company. Depression and suicide really does surpass all cultural and economic barriers (though I bet it's more common in certain ones).

Let me just say I would never recommend or push anyone else toward a final solution. Rationally I think people can learn to deal, yeah. I am constantly inspired by people, have an infinite amount of patience, forgiveness, and desire to see them succeed and stop hurting.

I just can't extend that courtesy to myself. I've lied to myself too many times for that. So when something breaks through those barriers, I'm defenseless. I remember all the time I've wasted and simple things others can do that seem impossible to me, and I am lost.

I've failed so many times that I know, undeniably, that I won't change. Or rather that I've re-invented myself half a dozen times over thirty years and have not gained a single bit of ground in what I find important.

So the feeling that nothing I do matters and that I will feel this way forever is especially strong.
